attacker.model: claude (Kiro subagent; exact model version not exposed to the agent)

cases.label: new password of 41 characters ending in a space: SQL Server truncates nvarchar(40), PostgreSQL text keeps the space
cases.reasoning: @NewPassword nvarchar(40) silently truncates a 41-character value to 40 on SQL Server, so HASHBYTES hashes 40 'n' + FullName. The conversion declares new_password text and hashes 40 'n' + ' ' + FullName, so the stored hash differs unless the conversion truncates too.

cases.label: old and new passwords differ only in case; the stored hash is compared as bytes
cases.reasoning: HASHBYTES comparison is binary (varbinary), so 'PW' and 'pw' hash to different values regardless of the database collation. The conversion compares bytea, which is also case-sensitive; a case-folding helper would wrongly match.

cases.label: two people share a full name and both have the same stored hash; only the requested PersonID changes
cases.reasoning: Person 2 and person 3 share FullName and HashedPassword; FullName 'Amy' vs 'amy' on person 1 tests that case is significant. The UPDATE must touch only PersonID = 2, leaving person 3 (same FullName) untouched on both engines.

top-ties.detail: two rows of Application.People share FullName = "amy"

cases.label: NULL new password with an empty-string preference present: hash becomes NULL, '' preference stays ''
cases.reasoning: @NewPassword NULL makes HASHBYTES(N'SHA2_256', NULL + FullName) NULL, so HashedPassword is set to NULL; the STRICT utf16le() with || NULL also yields NULL. Person 1's UserPreferences '' must stay '' (not become NULL), so '' and NULL are kept apart.

null-vs-empty.detail: empty string: yes; NULL in a text input: yes

cases.label: PersonID = 1 (the template) is refused even with the correct password; its row is unchanged
cases.reasoning: The WHERE has AND PersonID <> 1, so person 1 can never change. PersonIDs 1 and 3 (a gap) confirm the predicate is on the value, not row order; the conversion's PersonID <> 1 must behave the same and raise (nothing updated).

cases.label: a full name with a trailing space changes the hashed bytes
cases.reasoning: HashedPassword = HASHBYTES(..., @NewPassword + FullName) and FullName 'Ab ' keeps its trailing space; the conversion concatenates new_password || p."FullName" with the same trailing space. A conversion that rtrimmed the full name would store a different hash.

objections.text: The hand-derived 'old password differs only in case' case already tests binary hash comparison with a stored hash that actually matches the lowercase password. A02 supplies unrelated bytes (00ff10), so either case variant is refused and this is a weaker duplicate of that fixed case.

The stored hash aa is not SHA-256 over the UTF-16LE bytes of 'pwamy'. The password check therefore fails before any UPDATE, so the case cannot test its claim that only PersonID 2 changes while PersonID 3 stays untouched.

The stored hash 00ff10 is not the hash of 'pw' plus FullName 'x'. The call is refused, so HashedPassword does not become NULL as the label says. The hand-derived NULL-new-password case already reaches that assignment with a matching old-password hash.

The label says the supplied old password is correct, but the stored bytes 00ff10 are not the hash of 'pwroot'. The fixed case for PersonID 1 supplies a genuinely matching hash and already tests the template-person refusal.

The stored hash 00ff10 is not the hash of 'pw' plus the trailing-space FullName 'Ab '. The procedure raises before computing or storing the new hash, so removing the trailing space from the hashed full name would not change this case's outcome.

caught: no error when nothing was updated
missed: new password hashed without the full name

reasons: mutant adequacy is inadequate (unexplained misses: person 1 (the template) can change password, new password hashed without the full name, logon permission not re-enabled)
